sources.cite: Google Cloud, Associate Cloud Engineer certification exam guide: setting up (~20%), planning and configuring (~17.5%), deploying and implementing (~25%), ensuring successful operation (~20%), configuring access and security (~17.5%)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Bullets quoted: 4.5 'Working with Cloud DNS and Cloud NAT'; 3.5 'Creating ingress and egress firewall rules and policies'; 3.5 'Peering external networks (e.g., Cloud VPN, VPC Network Peering)'. The page shows five sections where the course seed has four units, and does not mention CMEK or Query Insights, which the seed's objectives do: a difference for the verification pass (finding in docs/sims.md 22.39).

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Set up and manage VPC Network Peering
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: gcloud compute networks peerings update accepts --export-custom-routes and --import-custom-routes; '--import-custom-routes tells the network to accept custom routes from the peered network'; for exports 'The peered network must be set to import the routes' and for imports 'The peered network must export the routes first'. That dynamic routes learned by Cloud Router are exchanged as custom routes, and that on-premises needs the peered VPC's range in Cloud Router's custom advertisements for the return path, are from memory of the routes and Cloud Router pages (to verify).
